messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @sara_oncall — Hosted API queue length on gpu-pool-3 exceeding 95% capacity, autoscaler throttle events detected. Trigger: queued_requests>10000 for 3m. Incident ID: INC-20260314-01

sara_oncall: on it. pulling up dashboards now.

mike_sre: i'm awake. what's the customer impact? any 5xxs?

ryan_support: seeing lots of timeouts from customers (timeout at 30s). Checks from tenant logs show repeated 504s and client retries. P95 latency jumped from 120ms to 3.8s, P99 ~12s.

ingrid_prod: also getting alerts from health checks — internal probe p50 is fine but p95 exploded. Some customers reporting 'rate limit exceeded' but upstream.

luis_prodops: looks like a traffic spike from a partner integration — sudden sustained QPS ~3x usual for sequence lengths 1024+. That combination kills token throughput.

sara_oncall: ok. first things first: is autoscaler failing to add nodes or are we hitting pool hard limit?

deploy-bot: autoscaler: attempt to scale nodegroup gpu-pool-3 +4 nodes -> failed: quota_exceeded: region-gpu-quota 16/16.

mike_sre: confirms: pool hit hard quota. We had reserved for other customers and can't provision more GPUs in region. Fallbacks should be activated.

sara_oncall: action list inbound: 1) enable degraded routing (route lower-cost model variant for non-SLA tenants), 2) enable global throttling to cap per-tenant QPS, 3) contact capacity team for emergency quota bump, 4) communicate to support and customers. I'll start 1 & 2.

sara_oncall: @deploy-bot please flip routing flag 'prefer-latency-over-quality' for tenant-group "public" (non-enterprise)

deploy-bot: config change queued. applying... DONE. routing: non-enterprise traffic -> model-7b-quant (previously 13b).

luis_prodops: already seeing drop in per-request GPU token cost, queue draining rate improved slightly. but high-priority enterprise tenants still stuck in queue.

mike_sre: enabling circuit breaker: 429 throttle for excessive prefix-heavy requests. Sara, put a conservative Retry-After=30.

sara_oncall: enabled throttles: policy "emergency_qps_cap" = 60r/s per tenant, response 429 with Retry-After:30.

ryan_support: posting status update to status.redwood.com: short note about degraded performance and partial mitigation. tagging impacted customers.

ingrid_prod: quick check of autoscaler logs — there's an exception when provisioning new instances: "insufficient capacity error: no GPU instances available in zone-a". Couple of retries then quota_exceeded.

mike_sre: so two problems: cloud quota + actual physical capacity shortage in zone. We'll want to failover to other regions if we can't get local capacity. But failover takes time and will break affinity for some customers.

sara_oncall: for immediate relief, can we evict lower-priority jobs on gpu-pool-3 to free slots?

luis_prodops: yes we can preempt spot-like batches: draining low-priority tasks now. Command: `rbctl pool drain --pool gpu-pool-3 --prio low --grace 30s`

mike_sre: do it.

luis_prodops: issued drain. low-priority workers terminating and work requeued into burst-cache. That should free ~6 GPUs worth of throughput in 2min.

sara_oncall: monitoring queue length...

(2m pass)

luis_prodops: queue length dropped 27% and token-per-second processing rose ~20%. P95 improved from 3.8s -> 1.2s for routed-to-7b traffic. Enterprise p95 still ~6s though.

ryan_support: customers seeing fewer timeouts but some still getting 504s. Adding note to the incident thread: partial mitigation applied, continue to monitor.

deploy-bot: autoscaler retrying provisioning in alternate zones... attempt -> failed: capacity_not_available.

mike_sre: I can open an emergency request with cloud capacity team and ask for temporary allocation, but ETA likely 30-90min if successful.

sara_oncall: ok. priority: keep drainage and throttles; prepare to failover enterprise traffic to dedicated-region-2 if cloud allocation doesn't arrive in 20m. Luis, can you coordinate the failover checklist?

luis_prodops: copying checklist: 1) ensure model artifacts exist in dedicated-region-2 registry, 2) pre-warm KV caches with recent prefixes, 3) update routing policy for enterprise tenant IDs, 4) enable cross-region egress and B2B keys. Starting step 1 now.

ingrid_prod: also flagging that dropping to 7b model affects output quality for a subset of prompts — we should mark this in customer comms.

sara_oncall: noted. Ryan, include fidelity degradation note in status post.

ryan_support: updated status: "We are experiencing a capacity-related degradation affecting higher-length workloads. Mitigations in place: degraded model routing and throttling. Enterprise customers may observe lower-quality responses or higher latency while we restore capacity. Next update in 30m or on major change."

(10m pass)

mike_sre: cloud team responded — they can free capacity with a cross-region lift but require action from our infra team and a verified business justification. Luis, can you raise the approval and I'll standby to execute?

luis_prodops: raising the request now with link to incident ID and expected QPS.

sara_oncall: meanwhile, I'm going to start a graceful on-call handoff note for @mike_sre in 20m. If the capacity ticket isn't cleared by then, assume handoff.

mike_sre: acknowledged. I'll be ready to take over at 1763502450 if needed.

(15m pass)

luis_prodops: cloud approved temporary allocation (EMERGENCY-ALLOTMENT 4 GPUs) — provisioning now.

deploy-bot: new nodes added to gpu-pool-3 +4 -> success.

sara_oncall: wow, nice. Watching queue drain...

luis_prodops: queue drained to normal thresholds in ~90s. P95 back to 140ms global, P99 ~400ms. Timeouts dropping.

ryan_support: pushed final customer update: "Capacity restored. Autoscaling hit quota during a traffic spike; we've applied throttles and degraded routing while adding emergency capacity. Monitoring closely. If you still see issues, reply to this post or open a ticket."

ingrid_prod: running post-incident checks: running evals for model-7b vs 13b on our regression prompts to quantify quality delta for the affected tenants.

mike_sre: prep postmortem notes: root cause = sudden high-QPS long-sequence traffic + regional GPU capacity limits + autoscaler blocked by quota. Contributing factors: lack of cross-region failover automation for enterprise tenants and no emergency quota playbook.

sara_oncall: handing off to @mike_sre in 15m. I'll update rotations and attach run commands I've run to the ticket. Good job everyone. :clap:

mike_sre: taking over. I'll draft a timeline and remediation actions: 1) automate cross-region failover, 2) add quota monitoring alerting earlier, 3) pre-approved emergency quota escalation path, 4) improve per-tenant cost/sequence detection to auto-degrade quality sooner.

luis_prodops: adding ops task: pre-warm standby pool in adjacent region during peak windows.

ryan_support: closing the incident channel on status site after the postmortem.

sara_oncall: incident resolved for now. I'll leave the thread open for any follow-ups.

(Hand-off metadata: original responder sara_oncall -> new owner mike_sre, handoff_ts=1763501489)
